messages:
Jared M: FYI ALB in us-west-2 started removing a bunch of edge targets ~10:15. Targets show HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED / timeout from the ALB side. Any recent changes?
Priya K: saw spikes in egress connections around that time — SNAT port usage on a few nodes hit 100% in the graphs. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion.
Alex R: Confirming logs from one affected pod:
```
10:14:51 GET /health 504 from 10.0.5.23 (alb)
10:14:52 readiness probe succeeded locally
10:14:53 kube-proxy: conntrack entries ~ 650k
```
SRE-bot: [ALERT] alb-target-group/edge-tg had 42 targets deregistered between 10:10-10:20 (cause: HC_TIMEOUT)
Jared M: Readiness probes on the pods are green, so looks like ALB can't reach them (timeouts), not app crash. ALB health checks originate from outside the VPC -> SNAT matters.
Priya K: We're still on iptables SNAT mode for aws-cni + host networking. Traffic to telemetry endpoint exploded (model telemetry + external artifact fetches) which would consume ephemeral ports.
Alex R: quick check: `ss -tn src :80 state established | wc -l` shows many outbound ephemeral bindings. conntrack shows a high SYN_RECV -> long TIME_WAIT piles.
Priya K: Mitigations I pushed: 1) scale up egress NAT gateway (added an extra nat gw in the AZ), 2) bumped conntrack_max and lowered conntrack timeout for ESTABLISHED on nodes. Not ideal but should free ports.
Jared M: Can we avoid SNAT for ALB healthchecks? If we set `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` on the service fronting the ALB, node preserves client IP and ALB would reach pod without SNAT from nodes that forward? Need to be careful w/ pod distribution.
Alex R: yep `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` would preserve source IP but you'd need nodePort on every node handling ALB. Risk: uneven pod distribution -> some nodes may stop serving. Alternatively use a dedicated egress gateway to route non-healthcheck egress through a separate path.
Priya K: For short term I also reduced health-check interval from 10s to 15s and increased healthy threshold to prevent flapping while we stabilize NAT. Not a permanent fix.
DeployBot: deploy/egress-scale-policy succeeded — autoscaler added 3 t3.medium NAT instances to the egress pool
Jared M: Thanks. Action items: Priya to monitor SNAT port usage and ALB target re-register rate, Alex to run a canary with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` on a small subset, SRE to add dashboard for node ephemeral port exhaustion.
SRE-bot: note: if we rely on `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` remember to set `proxy_protocol` on ALB if we want client IP preserved in app logs.
Priya K: current status — deregistrations stopped after NAT scale-up, ALB target count back to normal. Will follow up tomorrow with post-mortem and longer-term plan (egress gateway or per-AZ NATs). :thumbsup:
